title: CART: Clustering-based Analysis of Recurring narratives for Taxonomy construction
abstract: arXiv:2611.30993v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We present CART, a computational pipeline for extracting political narratives from parliamentary discourse and organizing them into a data-driven taxonomy without relying on predefined narrative categories. It encodes parliamentary discourse using semantic representations, filters relevant and reliable content through unsupervised confidence estimation, extracts narrative statements using LLMs, and uses narrative clustering and cluster analysis to construct a narrative taxonomy. Applied to Greek Parliament proceedings surrounding the 2023 Tempi train crash, it identifies ten recurring narrative families concerning responsibility attribution, institutional failure, railway safety, accountability, privatization, and the political interpretation of the tragedy. Our results demonstrate how combining unsupervised learning with LLM narrative extraction enables large parliamentary corpora to be transformed into interpretable, data-driven taxono

translated_title: CART：基于聚类的重复叙事分析以构建分类体系
translated_abstract: 我们提出了CART，这是一个计算流水线，用于从议会话语中提取政治叙事，并将其组织成数据驱动的分类体系，而无需依赖预定义的叙事类别。该系统使用语义表示对议会话语进行编码，通过无监督置信度估计过滤相关且可靠的内容，利用大语言模型提取叙事陈述，并通过叙事聚类和聚类分析构建叙事分类体系。将该系统应用于希腊议会围绕2023年坦皮火车事故的会议记录，它识别出十类重复出现的叙事家族，涉及责任归因、制度失灵、铁路安全、问责、私有化以及这一悲剧的政治解读。我们的结果表明，将无监督学习与大语言模型叙事提取相结合，能够将大规模议会语料库转化为可解释的、数据驱动的分类体系。
tldr: CART提出了一种无需预定义类别的计算流水线，将无监督学习与大语言模型叙事提取相结合，从议会话语中自动提取政治叙事并构建数据驱动的分类体系，在希腊议会关于2023年坦皮火车事故的辩论中识别出十类重复出现的叙事家族。
en_tdlr: CART introduces a computational pipeline that combines unsupervised learning with LLM-based narrative extraction to build data-driven narrative taxonomies from parliamentary discourse without predefined categories, identifying ten recurring narrative families from Greek Parliament debates on the 2023 Tempi train crash.
